# Code review: name schema rewritten to accept UTF-8 names

**Mode:** a fixed range, `c2a08710a...HEAD`. Findings were checked and scored, but only the top 2 went through the validate/refute agents.
**Scope:** 2 files, +128 −85 · base `c2a0871` → `c1b5d11` (committed only).
**Profile:** safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS · Zod + vitest · biome gates · 3 written rules in AGENTS.md (license headers, layering, pre-commit checks) · 7 of 9 areas have code to check.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fix #1 before opening the PR. #2 is a product decision to settle and record in the PR. |
| **Score** | About 76/100. This is an approximate figure: I used a simple deduction per finding (−15 for P2, −5 for P3), not the full scoring model. |
| **What held it down** | Names that show up blank still pass. The removed ASCII allow-list widens what can go into invite emails. |
| **Fix first** | #1: reject names that render as nothing. |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Bugs | 75 | 1 P2 · 2 P3 |
| Security | 85 | 1 P2 |
| Testing | 90 | 2 P3 |
| Simplicity | 90 | 2 P3 |
| Regression | 100 | The wider rules are intentional. Stored names still pass. Callers only use `.nullable()`, so they survive the change from `ZodString` to `ZodType<string>`. |
| Architecture | 100 | Nothing found. |
| Reuse | 100 | Nothing found. No existing NFC or `\p{Cf}` sanitizer anywhere in `src/`. |
| Performance | n/a | Linear in input size, and input is bounded by the request body limit. |
| Conventions | 100 | The SPDX header is present in both files. |

## What this review did not cover

- **Adjudication:** 2 of 9 findings went through a validator and a refuter. Both were confirmed and both stood. The other 7 I checked myself by running `node -e`, and they count at full weight.
- **Subagents:** you capped me at 2, so both went to adjudication. The category passes did not run as separate agents; I ran them all myself.
- **Not run:** tests, lint, and the "since your last run" comparison. I did not write `last-run.tsv`.
- **Out of scope:** web and mobile clients. I did not check whether they assume ASCII names.

## Fix before opening

**#1 · P2 · Bugs · `src/domain/common/schemas/name.schema.ts:13`** (also `:30`)
- **What's wrong:** `sanitizeName` only removes control (`Cc`) and format (`Cf`) characters. Characters that draw nothing but belong to other categories are kept. With the minimum now at 1, a name made only of one of them passes.
- **Confirmed inputs:** a bare U+200D (ZWJ) or U+200C (ZWNJ), U+3164 (Hangul filler), U+2800 (braille blank), U+FFA0, or a lone U+0301 (combining accent). Each comes out of the sanitizer as a 1-character string.
- **Why it matters:** your test "rejects a name that is empty after stripping" (`name.schema.spec.ts:108`) shows the goal is to reject invisible names, but this gets around it.
- **Where it reaches:** Space names (`space.entity.ts:22`), member aliases (`update-member-name.dto.entity.ts:7`), invite and accept-invite names, and address book names. Nothing further down the chain checks for this.
- **Fix:** after sanitizing, require at least one letter, number or symbol. For example, refine on `/[\p{L}\p{N}\p{S}]/u` after removing lone ZWJ/ZWNJ and the filler characters. Add these inputs to the spec.
- **Adjudication:** CONFIRMED (65) · STANDS.

**#2 · P2 · Security · `src/domain/common/schemas/name.schema.ts:29`**
- **What's wrong:** the old allow-list is gone. An inviter can now put `:`, `/`, full URLs and mixed-script lookalike characters into the invitee name and the workspace name.
- **Where it lands:** both values are written into the invite email Safe sends through SES (`space-invite-email.template.ts:36,101`). The invitee name can be up to 255 characters (`member.entity.ts:24`).
- **Proof:** the old regex rejected `"Click here: https://safe-claim.xyz/login"`. The new schema returns it unchanged.
- **What limits it:** the HTML is escaped, so this is not XSS. The call-to-action link is fixed on the server. Still, any user can create their own Space, become its admin and send these emails.
- **Fix, pick one:**
  - Keep Unicode, but reject URL-like text (`://`, `www.`) in fields that go into emails.
  - Leave the invitee's name out of the email.
  - Accept the risk and say so in the PR.
- **Adjudication:** CONFIRMED (40) · STANDS.

## Worth a ticket or a quick fix (P3)

| # | Area | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Bugs | `name.schema.ts:13` | Tag characters U+E0020–E007F are format characters, so the sanitizer strips them. That breaks subdivision flag emoji: 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 (Scotland) is quietly saved as a plain black flag 🏴. The fix is to exempt that range next to ZWJ and ZWNJ. |
| 4 | Bugs | `name.schema.ts:13` | Lone surrogates (`\p{Cs}`) are not stripped. `"\uD800"` passes validation, then UTF-8 encoding turns it into U+FFFD (`efbfbd`). The stored value is not the one that was validated. Add `\p{Cs}` to the list of removed characters. |
| 5 | Testing | `name.schema.spec.ts:116` | The test "rejects a name over max length (by code point)" uses ASCII `'abcd'`. If `[...s].length` were changed back to `s.length`, no test would fail. Add emoji right at the limit, such as 30 × 👍, which must pass. |
| 6 | Testing | `name.schema.spec.ts:273` | The assertion was weakened from `result.data === name` to `result.success`, so the sanitized output of that list is no longer checked. |
| 7 | Simplicity | `name.schema.ts:31,34` | The messages disagree: "at least 1 character(s)" vs "at most 30 characters". Clients that show these messages will see both styles. |
| 8 | Simplicity | `name.schema.spec.ts:95,99,104,110,345,349,354` and `name.schema.ts:10-11` | Invisible characters (U+202E, U+200B, U+200D, U+200C) are typed directly into the source. They can't be seen in review, which is the Trojan Source problem this change defends against. Write them as escapes: `'\u202E'`, `'\u200D'`. |

## Worth tidying while you're in these files

This is 2 proposals, about 4 lines. They have no score impact.

1. `name.schema.ts:4`: drop the history comment `// was 3 — …`; git already records it.
2. `name.schema.spec.ts:312-313`: the comment "passes, but … should still succeed" contradicts itself. Say plainly that an empty string is valid when `minLength` is 0.

**Your call:** for the two tidy-ups, reply fix, ticket or skip. Silence means skip. I haven't changed any files or posted anything.

## How this was produced

- **Diff:** `git diff c2a0871...c1b5d11`. I read it in full, plus every caller of `NameSchema`, `makeNameSchema` and `NAME_*` under `src/`, and the invite email template and service.
- **Checks:** I ran `node -e` with a copy of the sanitizer logic to confirm the inputs in #1, #3 and #4.
- **Adjudication:** one `finding-validator` and one `finding-refuter` each examined #1 and #2 on their own.
